title: What if spoiled eggs were zombies?
author: rectangle_so
selftext:
I'm building EggVerse, an arcade where I drop my egg characters into all kinds of different games & genuinely seeing my eggs in different scenarios & games has been hilarious and I'm having a lot of fun. 

For this one I thought, what if the egg started cracking as you took damage, but only fully cracked once you ran out of health?

Then I was like okay, what if the enemies were spoiled eggs... like zombies? andddd then it kind of spiraled from there. 

So here's Spoiled Egg its a wave-based zombie shooter, basically COD Zombies but with walking eggs instead.

You grab kitchen weapons from the spoiled eggs you crack (whisk blaster, hand mixer, fork launcher) & when you run out of ammo you have to fall back on your pea shooter.

Here is how I made it:

* Built with Claude Code as my coding agent, in TypeScript on a custom HTML5 canvas engine.
* I drew & designed the egg characters myself, and worked with a pixel artist years ago when I made my first game "Egg on the Run", I made 11 characters and the rest of the new art (zombie eggs, scenery, weapons etc) was generated using descriptive prompts I wrote to match the illustrative pixel-art style using Codex/ChatGPT.
* The part I struggled with the most was making it actually feel smooth on both desktop & mobile. Desktop was easy wherever your mouse is, you could shoot in that direction pressing space or clicking. On mobile I originally just had a shoot button & I was like okay... this is not smooth nor does it feel natural. So I ended up making two joysticks, one for moving & one for aiming/shooting and honestly it worked out great. 

Curious how other people building browser games handle mobile + desktop controls?

Anyway Spoiled Egg is live now for free @ eggverse.co or eggverse.co/games/spoiled-egg

You can play solo or open a room with up to 8 friends & see who survives the longest, would love to see who can get the highest wave 👀
